title: Construction Spending — Value of Construction Put in Place (March 2027 data), 10:00 a.m. ET — the same minute as ISM Manufacturing
source: EST: derived from the recovered C30 cadence, read direct from census.gov's own economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html on 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes) — the same primary the confirmed construction-spending-2026-12-01 entry cites, re-fetched rather than inherited. That page carries 2025 and 2026 rows only and publishes NO 2027 schedule, which is why this is EST: and not CENSUS:. What it does show is a series that broke and then repaired: the first half of 2026 ran a backlog with two reference months collapsed into single releases (January 21 2026 = Sep + Oct 2025 data; February 27 = Nov + Dec 2025; March 23 = Jan 2026; May 7 = Feb + Mar 2026), and from June 2026 the release returned to the first business day at 10:00 a.m. ET for SEVEN consecutive editions — 2026-06-01, 07-01, 08-03, 09-01, 10-01, 11-02, 12-01, every one of them that month's first business day. May 2027's first business day is Monday 2027-05-03 (2027-05-01 is a Saturday; no federal holiday; the NYSE trades a normal session). Filed estimate on three counts and all three are load-bearing: Census publishes no 2027 calendar, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the cadence it rests on was interrupted for five of the last nine months on the record — the recovery is seven prints old, not a decade. Discovered 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of ism-manufacturing-2027-05-03
notes: DISCOVERED as the tightest same-slot confound on this calendar: Construction Spending and ISM Manufacturing both release at 10:00 a.m. ET on the first business day, i.e. the SAME MINUTE, so no daily-bar study can ever separate them. The ism-manufacturing-2026-12-01 and -2027-02-01 ledgers both recorded that attribution problem in their honest-limits sections without ever filing the entry; the ism-manufacturing-2027-05-03 lane files it because the 2026 disruption makes it newly checkable. That is the entry's real value: for five months of 2026 the two prints did NOT share a session, which is the closest thing this calendar has to a natural experiment on a confound it has only ever assumed. A future session with the disrupted-window dates in hand can measure the ISM slot with and without Construction Spending in it. Impact LOW matches the three existing construction-spending entries. The residual risk is the cadence, not the day: a second backlog would move this by weeks, not hours, and would be visible on the Census calendar page months ahead. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
